==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈvaɪə/|/ˈviː.ə/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-I learned some phrases-via.wav|a=UK}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-via.oga|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪə|iːə|s=2}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weǵʰ-}}
[[File:Durchkontaktierung_IMGP3005.jpg|thumb|via (2) on a [[printed circuit board]]]]
{{bor+|en|la|via||road}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*weǵʰ-}}. Possible {{doublet|en|way|nocap=1}}.
The sense in electronics is also explained as ''vertical interconnect access''. <!--back-formation? if not, split ety.-->

====Noun====
{{en-noun|s|viae}}

# A main [[road]] or [[highway]], especially in ancient Rome. ''(Mainly used in set phrases, below.)''
# {{lb|en|electronics}} A small [[hole]] in a [[printed circuit board]] filled with [[metal]] which connects two or more [[layer]]s.
# {{lb|en|electronics}} An [[electrical]] [[connection]] which connects two or more [[layer]]s on a [[printed circuit board]] or an [[integrated circuit]].

===Etymology 2===
{{bor+|en|la|viā||by the way (of)}}, ablative singular of {{m|la|via||way, road}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*weǵʰ-}}.

Compare typologically {{m+|pl|drogą}}, {{m+|ru|путём}}.

====Alternative forms====
* {{alt|en|viâ}}

====Preposition====
{{en-head|prep}}

# {{U|by way of}}; passing through.
#: {{ux|en|They drove from New York to Los Angeles '''via''' Omaha.}}
#: {{ux|en|You can enter the building '''via''' the western gate.}}
# [[by means of|By (means of)]]; [[using]].
#: {{ux|en|I'll send you the information '''via''' e-mail.}}

A supplier many miles away would then take the part to the local matternet station for airborne dispatch '''via''' drone.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201062641/https://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21567193-networking-enthusiasts-dream-building-drone-powered-internet-carry-objects|archivedate=1 December 2017}}
